business: Passion4Growth: New-Market Sprint for logistics, wholesale and manufacturing companies in CEE (meetings with buyers in a new country or segment), run on the P4G outreach skill pack
by_segment: Commercial director at a manufacturer or exporter (EUR 10-50M revenue)
Founder or commercial director of a logistics, 3PL or freight forwarding firm
Owner of a wholesaler or distributor (EUR 2-10M revenue)
by_behaviour: Burned by an agency or consultant before
why_not: In freight, people give cargo to people they know and trust; a cold email from a warmed-up domain does not get me a shipper, my calls and the fairs do. I would maybe take the free 15-company sample out of curiosity, but I would not put EUR 1,500 down this month.

The split payment is clever and EUR 600 a meeting is fine on paper, but I paid an agency before and got nothing, so this month I would take the free 15-company sample and the 30-minute call, not sign. EUR 1,500 up front is still money I lose if the meetings are with people who never buy.

I'd probably take the free 15-company sample and then do the outreach myself with Apollo and Lemlist, which I already know how to run. EUR 3,000 for two months is real money for us when I think a junior SDR plus tools gets me most of the way there.

My buyers know me, they buy because I pick up the phone and shake hands at the fair. I might take the free 15-company sample out of curiosity, but I would not put EUR 1,500 down this month for cold emails from a Sofia agency.

We go into the new country next year, so I am not paying EUR 1,500 this month for meetings my team can't follow up yet. I would take the free sample of 15 companies, though, and use it to check whether they really understand our buyers.

I'd take the free 15-company sample, since it costs me nothing, but EUR 3,000 for what is basically Apollo plus Lemlist plus someone writing messages feels like a lot when I've run those tools myself. With two big customers cutting orders this quarter, I'm watching every euro before I hand it to an agency.
why_yes: Two big customers cut orders last quarter, so I need new buyers abroad and the trade fairs are not filling the gap. At EUR 3,000 for 5+ qualified meetings that is at most EUR 600 a meeting, less than one fair stand, and my real exposure is EUR 1,500 after I have already seen the 15-company sample.

We already have the plan for the new market and nobody on my team has time to open it, so a free sample of 15 targets and only EUR 1,500 at risk is easy to say yes to. I would take the sample first, and if those 15 companies are the right ones I would sign.
flip: If the 15-company sample names buyers I recognise as the right ones, and I can talk to a past manufacturing or export client about meetings that turned into orders, I would book a start date for Q1.
Talking directly to the past logistics client and hearing that those 45 meetings turned into signed freight contracts, not just calls, plus a sample list that names companies I don't already know.
